newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone suspends some diamond mining.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone suspends some diamond mining.

text.p: Sierra Leone's government has suspended diamond mining in a southern district where three hungry war orphans digging for wild yams stumbled on a flawless 100 carat stone worth an estimated $500,000.
State radio announced the move on Saturday but gave no reason. Sources close to the mineral resources ministry said the aim was to curb illegal diamond digging in the Pujehun district.
Thousands of people who fled fighting two years ago have returned to the region after December's peace deal between the government and rebels, who took up arms in 1991.
The orphans, whose parents were killed in a rebel attack on their village of Hinnah Malen two years ago, say they found the diamond nestling under a yam near the village on Tuesday.
Morie Jah, 14, the oldest boy, told reporters they had gone out early after two days without food but decided to return home hungry after searching in vain for yams for three hours.
Valuers at the government gold and diamond office in the capital Freetown said the stone was worth at least $500,000
The government has not commented on the find.
It was not immediately clear what the children had got for the diamond.
Some reports from Bo, the nearest large town, suggested a Lebanese diamond trader had given them bicycles, personal stereo players and food. Other reports suggested he paid them cash.
